summary: The UNESCO/Japan Young Researchers' Fellowships Programme (also called the UNESCO/Keizo Obuchi Research Fellowships) was set up in 2001 under the Japanese Funds-in-Trust, with the support of the Government of Japan. In Cycle 2026 it gives 10 fellowships to young researchers from Africa, Small Island Developing States, Ukraine and Turkiye for 3 to 9 months of postgraduate research at a Japanese university or research institution. The research must fall in heritage conservation and management or one of four artificial intelligence areas. The grant is a lump sum of up to US$10,000.
eligibility_notes:
Nationality: you must be a national of an invited Member State or Associate Member. Annex 1 lists 83 Member States and 8 Associate Members: Africa (47 Member States), the Arab States (Bahrain), Asia and the Pacific (17 Member States and 2 Associate Members, New Caledonia and Tokelau), Latin America and the Caribbean (16 Member States and Associate Members Anguilla, Aruba, British Virgin Islands, Cayman Islands, Curacao, Montserrat and Sint Maarten) and Europe (Turkiye and Ukraine). Annex 1 says these include 48 Small Island Developing States.

Age: no more than 40 years old at the time of application.

Qualifications: at least a master's degree (or equivalent) in a field relevant to the proposed research, and strong academic and research potential. Prospective diploma winners must give official proof of student status.

Language: enough reading and writing proficiency in the language of instruction or supervision at the proposed host institution in Japan.

Host: acceptance from an academic supervisor at a Japanese university or research institution who will oversee the research.

Each invited country or territory may submit at most two candidates, and at least one should be a woman. Only applications endorsed by the National Commission for UNESCO are considered; incomplete or late applications and candidates who do not meet eligibility are not considered.
age_experience_notes: Maximum age 40 at the time of application. No minimum years of work experience is stated; the entry qualification is a master's degree or equivalent.
funding_summary: A lump-sum grant of up to US$10,000 for a research stay in Japan of no less than 3 and no more than 9 months, between February 2027 and December 2027. It is meant to cover only costs tied to the approved research: international and domestic travel for the approved itinerary, accommodation, medical insurance, personal subsistence (meals, local transport, incidentals) and other research-related costs where relevant. Medical insurance is mandatory and arranged by UNESCO; its cost (about US$75 per month, US$225 to US$675 in total) is deducted before the money is paid out. Tuition, equipment (including computers) and publication costs are not eligible, and conference participation only when clearly part of the research.
programmes_note: Proposals must fall under one primary research area and one matching sub-area from Annex 2: (1) Heritage Conservation and Management, (2) AI for Sustainable Management of Natural Resources and Climate Action, (3) Ethical, Inclusive and Human-Centred AI for Sustainable Development, (4) AI for Sustainable Cities, Infrastructure and Societal Resilience, (5) AI and Education. UNESCO is interested in interdisciplinary work that links these themes to social, ethical and governance questions. Annex 2 holds 28 indicative sub-areas; the first 25 are listed under the level.
institutions_note: A Japanese university or research institution that accepts you under an academic supervisor. You must obtain the acceptance letter yourself. The programme is run by UNESCO with the Government of Japan (Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Permanent Delegation of Japan to UNESCO and the Japanese National Commission for UNESCO). No list of host institutions is published on the pages read.

summary.detail: The official pages call this 'postgraduate research' by young researchers with at least a master's degree (age 40 or under). They do not use the word postdoctoral, and a doctorate is not required, so this level is kept as stored but is not confirmed. Duration 3 to 9 months in Japan between February 2027 and December 2027, under an academic mentor. The language of the stay is the language of instruction or supervision at the host institution. Research areas are the five above; 25 of the 28 sub-areas are listed here.

benefits.limit_text: Lump-sum grant of up to US$10,000 for the research stay
benefits.conditions: For costs directly tied to the approved research stay in Japan, 3 to 9 months. The budget in your proposal must be in US dollars and must not exceed US$10,000.

benefits.limit_text: International and domestic travel for the approved itinerary, paid from the grant
benefits.conditions: Not a separate payment: it comes out of the US$10,000 lump sum.

benefits.limit_text: Accommodation in Japan, paid from the grant
benefits.conditions: Not a separate payment: it comes out of the lump sum.

benefits.limit_text: Personal subsistence (meals, local transport, incidentals), paid from the grant
benefits.conditions: Not a separate payment: it comes out of the lump sum.

benefits.limit_text: Medical insurance is mandatory, arranged by UNESCO. Estimated about US$75 per month, US$225 to US$675 in total
benefits.conditions: The cost is deducted from the grant before payment, so fellows receive the balance.

benefits.limit_text: Equipment (including computers), publication costs and conference participation
benefits.conditions: Conference participation is allowed only if clearly justified as an integral part of the research with a direct and significant contribution. UNESCO does not pay for publishing the results.

requirements.text: Fellowship application form on the official UNESCO template (Annex 3), completed in English or French.
Certified copies of diplomas. Documents in other languages need a notarised English or French translation.
requirements.conditional_rule: Prospective diploma winners give official proof of student status from their current institution

requirements.text: Academic transcripts, with a notarised English or French translation if in another language.
One letter of recommendation from a referee familiar with your research or professional work.
Letter of acceptance from the Japanese host institution, confirming it will receive you and provide supervision and research facilities in your field.

Proof of proficiency in the language of instruction or supervision of the proposed research: an official certificate such as IELTS, TOEFL, JLPT or another recognised test. If you have none, the UNESCO Certificate of Language Knowledge (Annex 5), completed, signed and stamped by a certified language institution or tutor.

Research proposal on the Annex 4 template, in English or French, no more than 3 pages: description of the research, expected results, implementation plan and a budget in US dollars. It must name one primary research area and its sub-area from Annex 2 and state a duration of 3 to 9 months.
Letter of nomination from your National Commission for UNESCO, sent with the application.

application_steps.title: Read the guide and contact your National Commission
application_steps.detail: Check that your country is on the Annex 1 list and that you meet the age, degree and language rules. Ask your National Commission for UNESCO about its national selection process; only endorsed applications are considered. The programme page asks you to give your Commission the documents at least two weeks before the deadline.

application_steps.title: Find a Japanese supervisor and prepare the documents
application_steps.detail: Obtain an acceptance letter from an academic supervisor at a Japanese university or research institution. Prepare the form, certified diplomas, transcripts, recommendation letter, language proof and a research proposal of up to 3 pages with a budget of no more than US$10,000, covering 3 to 9 months.

application_steps.title: Submit through your National Commission before the deadline
application_steps.detail: The National Commission sends the nomination letter and all documents to UNESCO by email. The application guide gives 30 September 2026 (midnight, Paris time); the programme page, updated 28 September 2026, says the deadline was extended to 15 October 2026 (midnight, Paris time). Each country may nominate up to two candidates, at least one a woman. Incomplete or late applications are not considered.

application_steps.title: Evaluation by a UNESCO and Japan expert committee
application_steps.detail: A Selection Committee of UNESCO and Government of Japan experts in the relevant fields assesses the merit of the candidate and the quality, relevance and originality of the research. The guide plans evaluation for October and November 2026.

application_steps.title: Final decision by the Japanese authorities
application_steps.detail: The Japanese authorities decide, based on the committee's recommendation, with attention to gender equality and diversity. Fellowships are awarded in December 2026. Successful candidates receive an official Letter of Award from UNESCO; a candidate who has heard nothing by 31 January 2027 should treat the application as unsuccessful.

application_steps.title: Research stay in Japan
application_steps.detail: The research stay lasts 3 to 9 months, starting in February 2027 or later and finishing no later than December 2027, under the supervision of an academic mentor at the host institution. UNESCO arranges the mandatory medical insurance and takes its cost from the grant before paying the rest.

application_steps.title: Reports and sharing the results
application_steps.detail: Fellows submit an interim report at the halfway point and a final report at the end, plus a one-page summary of the outcomes for UNESCO communication. They are encouraged to share the results; no prior UNESCO approval is needed to publish, but publications should acknowledge UNESCO, the programme and the Government of Japan, and a copy should be sent to UNESCO.

not_stated: A list of Japanese host institutions, or help in finding a supervisor
Teaching or supervision language at hosts (it depends on the host)
The payment schedule of the lump sum (only that insurance is deducted before disbursement)
Any visa support or residence arrangements in Japan
Any obligation to return to the home country
fetch_problems: Annex 3 (application form), Annex 4 (proposal template) and Annex 5 (language certificate) were not opened; their content was taken from the application guide and the programme page.
A direct download of the guide and annexes from the UNESCO site was blocked by a browser check in a scripted download; the PDFs were read through the page fetch tool instead. No bypass was attempted.
notes: The application guide (published 6 July 2026) gives a deadline of 30 September 2026 and results by 31 January 2027; the programme page (updated 28 September 2026) says the deadline was extended to 15 October 2026. Both are stated above.
The nationality list stored (about 88 entries) is carried over from stored data. Annex 1 lists 83 Member States and 8 Associate Members; it was not diffed entry by entry.
The programme page names the host language rule as 'language of instruction or supervision at the host institution'; the stored text said 'language of the Japanese host'.

Annex 1's heading counts 8 Associate Members in total (6 for Latin America and the Caribbean) but seven territories are named under Latin America and the Caribbean, as the programme page also says; the named list is used.
Stored milestone 'Award of fellowships: December 2026' agrees with the guide.
